ingredientSections.heading: Kimchi
items: Brine, 2-3 litres water, ⅓-½ cup Kosher Salt

methodSections.heading: Kimchi
steps: In a large pot, heat the water and dissolve the salt to create the brine. Allow to cool.
Trim the cabbage and cut into quarters. Cut out the core and cut each quarter into 3-4cm chunks. Place in a large bowl or bucket and add enough brine to submerge the cabbage.
Cover with plastic wrap and let sit at room temperature for 12 to 24 hours.
Combine the remaining ingredients in a bowl and allow the mixture to sit for at least 15 minutes at room temperature.
Thoroughly drain the cabbage. Combine with the flavouring mixture ensuring all the cabbage is well coated.

Pack into a clean two litre jar that can be well sealed. Make sure to include all of the liquid from the mixture. Allow to ferment at room temperature in a dark place for at least 24 hours or longer, until there is noticeable bubbling. Remove the lid to allow gasses to escape once or twice during this time.

After the desired level of fermentation is reached, place the jar in the fridge. Fermentation will continue at lower temperatures but much more slowly. It will keep for at least a month but will get more and more potent.

methodSections.heading: Ribs
steps: Bring together all of the marinade ingredients, blend into a puree, and set aside.
Layout the cut short ribs and liberally coat in the marinade. Cover with plastic wrap and allow to marinate in the fridge for 12 hours.

Fire up the grill to a high heat. When it reaches roughly 230°C (450°F), grill the marinated short ribs for about five minutes on each side. When cooked remove from heat and slice into smaller portions between the bones.
